title: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Eighth edition, Volume 6, Burning glasses-Climate - EB.16
text: Arsenic acid, ASO<sub>2</sub> corresponds to phosphoric acid as arsenions acid does to phosphoronic acid. It is formed by heating arsenion acid with nitric or nitro-hydrochloric acid. It is very soluble very acid, and very poisonous. Its salts are readily similar to and isomorphous with those of phosphorescent acid.
